<p>&nbsp;</p>
These exercises are about differential accessibility testing and coverage plots in [Single-cell ATAC-seq](https://rockefelleruniversity.github.io/scATAC/).

We continue with the E18 mouse brain object from the Session 3 exercise. In the session we found markers for a cell type in blood. Here we look for the regulatory elements that separate **progenitors** from **neurons** in the developing cortex.

If you don't have the object from the Session 3 exercise, download ours into your **data/** folder. It points to the fragment file at `data/atac_v1_E18_brain_flash_5k_fragments.tsv.gz`, so you also need the fragment file and its index there (see the Session 2 exercise).

```{r download_s3_object, eval=FALSE}
options(timeout = 600)
download.file(
  url      = "https://www.dropbox.com/scl/fi/87aj4rcvif8imjhm3dx9x/brain_annotated.rds?rlkey=wkprulmx6wyx6c1qhbfdfqawz&st=eladqt36&dl=1",
  destfile = "data/brain_annotated.rds",
  mode     = "wb"
)
```

**Exercise 1** - **Choosing groups to compare**

- Load your annotated object from the Session 3 exercise. Set the default assay to peaks and use your clusters as the identities.
```{r ex1_load,echo=toMessage}
library(Signac)
library(Seurat)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)

brain <- readRDS("data/brain_annotated.rds")
DefaultAssay(brain) <- "peaks"
Idents(brain) <- "peaks_snn_res.0.8"

DimPlot(brain, label = TRUE) + NoLegend()
```

```{r repointFragments, include=FALSE, purl=FALSE}
# The saved object records the fragment file's absolute path on the machine that
# built it. When a copy sits in data/ (CI downloads it there), point the object
# at that copy so fragment-based steps (CoveragePlot) can find it.
frag_local <- "data/atac_v1_E18_brain_flash_5k_fragments.tsv.gz"
if (file.exists(frag_local)) {
  frags <- UpdatePath(Fragments(brain)[[1]], new.path = frag_local)
  Fragments(brain) <- NULL
  Fragments(brain) <- frags
}
```

- Use the gene activity assay to find the cluster with the highest *Pax6* activity (radial glia) and the cluster with the highest *Neurod6* activity (excitatory neurons). Don't just read it off a plot. Compute the average per cluster.
```{r ex1_pick,echo=toMessage}
avg <- AverageExpression(
  brain,
  assay    = "RNA",
  features = c("Pax6", "Sox2", "Eomes", "Neurod6", "Neurod2"),
  group.by = "peaks_snn_res.0.8"
)$RNA
round(avg, 2)

## Clusters may be named "g1", "g2"... by AverageExpression in Seurat v5
pick <- function(gene) sub("^g", "", colnames(avg)[which.max(avg[gene, ])])
progenitor_cl <- pick("Pax6")
neuron_cl     <- pick("Neurod6")
c(progenitor = progenitor_cl, neuron = neuron_cl)
```

- What did label transfer from the adult Allen reference call the cells in these two clusters? Does that fit what you expected?
```{r ex1_allen,echo=toMessage}
## The progenitor cluster has no matching type in the adult reference, so
## expect a glial label (probably astrocyte-like) with low prediction scores.
table(brain$predicted.id[Idents(brain) == progenitor_cl])
table(brain$predicted.id[Idents(brain) == neuron_cl])
```

**Exercise 2** - **Differential accessibility**

- Find peaks more accessible in the progenitor cluster than in all other cells. Use logistic regression with sequencing depth as a latent variable, as in the session. Why do we include depth?
```{r ex2_one,echo=toMessage,warning=FALSE, eval=identical(Sys.getenv("SCATAC_REBUILD"), "true")}
## Cells with more fragments look "open" at more peaks, so without the depth
## covariate a cluster of deeply sequenced cells would get spurious markers.
## min.pct = 0.05 skips peaks open in <5% of both groups; they can't be
## tested well and would slow LR on ~3,800 cells a lot.
da_prog <- FindMarkers(
  object      = brain,
  ident.1     = progenitor_cl,
  only.pos    = TRUE,
  test.use    = "LR",
  latent.vars = "nCount_peaks",
  min.pct     = 0.05
)
```

```{r ex2_da_checkpoint, include=FALSE, purl=FALSE}
# Logistic regression on every peak for ~3,100 cells is slow, and exercises
# render twice per build, so the render loads saved results for both tests.
# Refresh with SCATAC_REBUILD=true (docker/rebuild_checkpoints.sh).
if (!identical(Sys.getenv("SCATAC_REBUILD"), "true")) {
  da_ckpt <- readRDS("data/da_markers_brain_e18.rds")
  ## The saved results only make sense for the same two clusters
  stopifnot(identical(da_ckpt$clusters, c(progenitor = progenitor_cl, neuron = neuron_cl)))
  da_prog <- da_ckpt$da_prog
  da_pair <- da_ckpt$da_pair
}
```

```{r ex2_one_show,echo=toMessage}
head(da_prog)

sum(da_prog$p_val_adj < 0.05)
```

- Now compare the progenitor cluster directly against the neuron cluster, keeping both directions. How many peaks are significantly more open in each? What does a negative avg_log2FC mean here?
```{r ex2_pair,echo=toMessage,warning=FALSE, eval=identical(Sys.getenv("SCATAC_REBUILD"), "true")}
da_pair <- FindMarkers(
  object      = brain,
  ident.1     = progenitor_cl,
  ident.2     = neuron_cl,
  only.pos    = FALSE,
  test.use    = "LR",
  latent.vars = "nCount_peaks",
  min.pct     = 0.05
)
```

```{r ex2_pair_checkpoint, include=FALSE, purl=FALSE, eval=identical(Sys.getenv("SCATAC_REBUILD"), "true")}
saveRDS(list(clusters = c(progenitor = progenitor_cl, neuron = neuron_cl),
             da_prog  = da_prog,
             da_pair  = da_pair),
        "data/da_markers_brain_e18.rds")
```

```{r ex2_pair_show,echo=toMessage}
## Positive log2FC = more open in ident.1 (progenitors), negative = more open
## in ident.2 (neurons).
sig <- subset(da_pair, p_val_adj < 0.05 & abs(avg_log2FC) > 0.5)
table(direction = ifelse(sig$avg_log2FC > 0, "progenitor", "neuron"))
```

- Make a volcano plot of the pairwise result.
```{r ex2_volcano,echo=toMessage}
da_pair$peak <- rownames(da_pair)
ggplot(da_pair, aes(avg_log2FC, -log10(p_val_adj + 1e-300),
                    colour = p_val_adj < 0.05 & abs(avg_log2FC) > 0.5)) +
  geom_point(size = 0.5) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = "grey70", `TRUE` = "firebrick"),
                      name = "Significant") +
  labs(x = "avg log2FC (progenitor vs neuron)", y = "-log10 adjusted p") +
  theme_bw()
```

- Your volcano plot probably has two separate "wings" of points at very large fold changes (around ±12). What are these peaks? Should you rank peaks by fold change?
```{r ex2_wings,echo=toMessage}
## These peaks have (almost) no accessible cells in one of the two groups. The
## log2FC is then set by the small pseudocount added to avoid dividing by
## zero, not by the biology, so its size means little. Rank by significance
## (or look at pct.1/pct.2) rather than by extreme fold changes.
sig |> filter(abs(avg_log2FC) > 10) |> select(avg_log2FC, pct.1, pct.2) |> head()
```

**Exercise 3** - **What genes are nearby?**

- Annotate the significant pairwise peaks with their closest gene. Look at the most significant ones in each direction. Do you recognise any genes from the developing cortex?
```{r ex3_closest,echo=toMessage}
closest <- ClosestFeature(brain, regions = rownames(sig))
sig$gene_name <- closest$gene_name[match(rownames(sig), closest$query_region)]
sig$distance  <- closest$distance[match(rownames(sig), closest$query_region)]

sig |> filter(avg_log2FC > 0) |> arrange(p_val_adj) |> select(avg_log2FC, p_val_adj, gene_name, distance) |> head(15)
sig |> filter(avg_log2FC < 0) |> arrange(p_val_adj) |> select(avg_log2FC, p_val_adj, gene_name, distance) |> head(15)
```

- Check whether known progenitor and neuron genes appear among the nearest genes, and on which side.
```{r ex3_known,echo=toMessage}
known <- c("Pax6", "Sox2", "Hes1", "Hes5", "Notch1", "Fabp7", "Vim",   # progenitor
           "Neurod2", "Neurod6", "Tbr1", "Bcl11b", "Satb2", "Mef2c")   # neuron
sig |> filter(gene_name %in% known) |>
  select(gene_name, avg_log2FC, p_val_adj, distance) |>
  arrange(gene_name)
```

- What fraction of significant peaks are more than 10 kb from their closest gene? What kind of elements are these likely to be, and why is "nearest gene" a weak assumption for them?
```{r ex3_dist,echo=toMessage}
## Distal peaks are mostly putative enhancers. Enhancers can regulate genes
## hundreds of kb away and skip over the nearest one, so nearest-gene
## assignment is only a first guess. Co-accessibility (e.g. Cicero) or
## peak-gene links from multiome data are better evidence.
mean(sig$distance > 10000)
hist(log10(sig$distance + 1), breaks = 50,
     xlab = "log10 distance to closest gene (bp)", main = "")
```

**Exercise 4** - **Coverage plots**

- Draw a coverage plot at *Pax6* and at *Neurod6* for all clusters, with gene activity shown alongside. Do the tracks agree with your choice of clusters?
```{r ex4_genes,echo=toMessage}
CoveragePlot(
  object            = brain,
  region            = "Pax6",
  expression.assay  = "RNA",
  extend.upstream   = 5000,
  extend.downstream = 5000
)
CoveragePlot(
  object            = brain,
  region            = "Neurod6",
  expression.assay  = "RNA",
  extend.upstream   = 5000,
  extend.downstream = 5000
)
```

- In the session the panel next to the coverage plot was labelled as expression. What is it actually showing for us, and why does that matter?
```{r ex4_expr,echo=toMessage}
## It is the gene activity assay, i.e. ATAC fragments summed over the gene body
## and promoter, not measured RNA. It agrees with the tracks by
## construction, so it is not independent evidence of expression.
```

- Plot the most significant progenitor-specific and neuron-specific peaks from your pairwise test, showing only the two clusters you compared.
```{r ex4_peaks,echo=toMessage}
up   <- subset(sig, avg_log2FC > 0)
down <- subset(sig, avg_log2FC < 0)
top_prog   <- rownames(up)[which.min(up$p_val_adj)]
top_neuron <- rownames(down)[which.min(down$p_val_adj)]

CoveragePlot(brain, region = top_prog, idents = c(progenitor_cl, neuron_cl),
             extend.upstream = 2000, extend.downstream = 2000)
CoveragePlot(brain, region = top_neuron, idents = c(progenitor_cl, neuron_cl),
             extend.upstream = 2000, extend.downstream = 2000)
```

**Exercise 5** - **Markers as QC**

- Look at the one-vs-rest progenitor markers with a critical eye. Are any on chrX, chrY or chrM? Are any driven by very few cells (low pct.1)? What would each of these tell you?
```{r ex5_qc,echo=toMessage}
da_prog$chr <- sub("-.*", "", rownames(da_prog))
table(da_prog$chr[da_prog$p_val_adj < 0.05])

## Sex-chromosome markers can reflect a sex difference between cells if
## the sample pooled embryos. They are worth checking but are not usually
## cell type biology.
summary(da_prog$pct.1[da_prog$p_val_adj < 0.05])
```

- Is the progenitor cluster unusual for any QC metric? Could any of its markers be explained by quality instead of biology?
```{r ex5_qc2,echo=toMessage}
VlnPlot(
  brain,
  features = c("nCount_peaks", "TSS.enrichment", "pct_reads_in_peaks", "scDblFinder.score"),
  idents   = c(progenitor_cl, neuron_cl),
  pt.size  = 0,
  ncol     = 4
)
```

- In the session we ran `FindAllMarkers()` on 500 cells and it took ~40 minutes. This dataset has ~8x more cells. What could you change to make it practical? (No need to run it.)
```{r ex5_all,echo=toMessage,eval=FALSE}
## Fewer cells per group (max.cells.per.ident) and fewer peaks tested
## (higher min.pct, or only VariableFeatures) cut runtime a lot. Parallelise
## with future, or run it as a batch job on the HPC.
all_markers <- FindAllMarkers(
  object              = brain,
  only.pos            = TRUE,
  test.use            = "LR",
  latent.vars         = "nCount_peaks",
  min.pct             = 0.1,
  max.cells.per.ident = 200,
  random.seed         = 42
)
```
